newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close 2.58 pct down on default rumour.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close 2.58 pct down on default rumour.

text.p: Thai stocks ended down 2.58 percent in moderate trade on Thursday after investors sold stocks heavily in the afternoon on rumours that some brokerages were hit by client defaults on margin loans, brokers said.

The SET index which fell for the sixth consecutive trading day dropped 27.06 points to 1,022.68 on 5.2 billion baht trade. Decliners trounced gainers 353 to 45 while 73 issues were unchanged. The SET-50 index fell 2.28 points to 77.44.
"The rumours which began spreading in the market soon after the session resumed in the afternoon made investors jitters," said Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.
The SET, which has been battered this week following the new Iraq-U.S. crisis and Moody's Investors Services downgrading of Thailand's short-term rating, was further hurt by the rumours.
A statement from the Thai bourse denying the rumours failed to lift the market gloom. Brokers expected that the rumours would continue to affect sentiment in the stock market tomorrow as well.
Prices of some finance and brokerage firms coumnters fell down the 10 percent limit on the rumours.
"The key psychological barrier of the index now stands at 1,000. It's a strong support and nobody wants to see it breached," Virat said.
"Poor sentiment is expected to persist tomorrow as every newspaper will report them (rumours). The index is expected to fall further," Virat said.
Finance One topped the active list, falling four baht to 97, Bangkok Bank slipped two to 210, Electricity Generating fell 1.50 to 70.50, and Dhana Siam declined three to 102.
